tasks.title: Design PostgreSQL schema and migrations (users, roles, products, stock, movements, suppliers, thresholds, purchase orders)
Set up Node.js REST API, React PWA shell, TLS config, CI and role-aware bottom navigation
Build login, JWT auth with bcrypt, and RBAC middleware on every endpoint
Create UI kit and mobile-first screen designs (Scan, Product Detail, Alerts, Dashboard, Reports, Team) at 360px with accessibility
Implement product lookup and create endpoints with indexed barcode search (under 1 second)
Build Scan and Lookup screen with ZXing camera scanning, handheld scanner input, manual entry, unknown barcode prompt and Receive Delivery batch mode
Implement stock adjustment API with reason codes, transactional audit log (user, timestamp, reason) and receive-delivery endpoint
Add WebSocket broadcast of stock changes and live-updating Product Detail and Dashboard counters (under 2 seconds)
Build Product Detail and Adjust Stock screen with stepper, reason selector, movement history and threshold input
Implement threshold-based low-stock detection and in-app alerts pushed to managers via WebSocket
Build Low-Stock Alerts screen with supplier grouping and draft purchase order generation API and modal
Implement dashboard and report aggregation queries (stock value, low-stock counts, top sellers, turnover) and CSV export endpoint
Build Dashboard and Reports screens with date range picker, charts and CSV download
Build Team and Roles screens: create staff, role assignment, deactivate user, failed-login logging and access-denied state
Run load test for 50 concurrent users, configure daily automated backups, PWA install check and end-to-end acceptance tests

risks: Camera barcode scanning (ZXing) may be slow or unreliable on low-end phones or in poor lighting, threatening the 1-second lookup target; mitigate with manual entry and handheld scanner fallback.
Real-time WebSocket sync within 2 seconds can break under flaky store Wi-Fi or concurrent edits; mitigate with reconnect logic, transactional updates and server-authoritative counts.
Scope is large for a small team; F3 purchase orders and F4 reports are lower priority and should be cut to basic versions if the schedule slips.
No offline support in the MVP means scans during connectivity loss may be lost; mitigate with clear sync status and retry queue if time allows.
Security and RBAC gaps (endpoint coverage, deactivated-user sessions) could slip through under time pressure; mitigate with centralized middleware and automated permission tests.
